desc: The Varginha case is the only Latin American event that alleges the full sequence this board is built around: a crash, a recovery, custody of biological material, and an American removal. On 13 January 1996, outside Varginha in Minas Gerais, geography teacher and ultralight pilot Carlos de Sousa reported seeing a cylindrical craft trailing smoke come down near a highway; he says he reached the site, smelled ammonia and rotten eggs, picked up a metal fragment that sprang back to shape after he crushed it, and was driven off at gunpoint by soldiers who arrived within minutes. On 20 January 1996 at about 15:20 three young women - Liliane Silva, then 14, her sister Valquíria, 16, and their friend Kátia Xavier, 21 - reported encountering a crouching brown, oily-skinned creature with red eyes, three fingers and a large head in a vacant lot on Rua Dr. Benevenuto Braz Vieira. In 2010 an official Brazilian military inquiry concluded the young women had seen a mentally disabled man nicknamed 'Mudinho', Luiz Antônio de Paula, and that the military vehicle movements were routine maintenance and Fire Brigade activity misinterpreted. Thirty years later the case reached the United States Congress.

timeline.label: The Varginha encounter
timeline.text: Three young women in Varginha, Minas Gerais report a crouching creature with red eyes and three fingers; a week earlier an ultralight pilot reported a cylindrical craft coming down outside the town. Rumours of military recovery and of an American removal follow. A 2010 Brazilian military inquiry attributes the sighting to a mentally disabled man and routine vehicle movements.

timeline.label: Brazilian Army inquiry on Varginha
timeline.text: The inquiry concludes the 1996 witnesses encountered Luiz Antonio de Paula, a mentally disabled man, and that the observed military vehicle movements were routine maintenance and Escola de Sargentos das Armas transport. The underlying unit movement logs are not published.
